title: What I Eat in a Day Training for My First Half Ironman
creator: Priya Runs Things
description:
A full training day, 6 weeks out from my first 70.3: early swim, a long bike on the trainer, and everything I ate (about 3,400 calories).

My training plan and race recap are coming soon!

Instagram: @priyarunsthings
Strava: Priya K.

sentences.t: Good morning, it is five fifteen, and today is one of my biggest training days of the week.
I'm six weeks out from my first half Ironman, so today is a swim this morning and a three-hour bike this afternoon.
A lot of you asked what I actually eat on days like this, so I'm bringing you along for the whole thing.
First thing before the swim is something small and easy, so a banana and a spoonful of peanut butter.
I can't swim on a full stomach, I've tried, and it ends badly.
Coffee, obviously, just black, and a big glass of water with an electrolyte tab in it.
Okay, we're at the pool, and it's my favourite time, because it's almost empty.
Today is three kilometres with some threshold sets in the middle, so I'll see you on the other side.
That was hard, those last two hundreds were brutal, and I am starving.
So, breakfast number two, and this is where today's sponsor comes in, Oatbound.
Oatbound makes protein oats, so it's rolled oats with twenty-five grams of protein per serving, no weird aftertaste, and nothing artificial.
I've been having them after almost every morning session for the last two months, because I genuinely don't have time to cook a proper breakfast between training and work.
You just add hot water or milk, give it a stir, and it's ready in about two minutes.
My favourite flavour is the cinnamon apple, but the salted caramel one is dangerously good.
If you want to try them, use code PRIYA20 at oatbound.com for twenty percent off your first order, and they ship to most of Europe and North America.
I throw some frozen blueberries on top, and that's breakfast.
Then I work from about nine until one, and I snack a lot during that, mostly yogurt, some crackers and an apple.
Lunch is the big one before the bike, so I want a lot of carbs but nothing that sits too heavy.
This is rice, some salmon I made last night, cucumber, soy sauce and a fried egg on top.
I try to eat this about two hours before getting on the bike so it has time to settle.
Okay, bike time, this is three hours on the trainer, which honestly is more mentally hard than physically hard.
Fueling on the bike is something I really got wrong at the start, I used to barely eat anything and then completely fall apart.
Now I aim for about sixty to seventy grams of carbs every hour, so that's a mix of drink mix, gels and these little rice cakes I make.
And I set a timer every twenty minutes, because I will absolutely forget otherwise.
Done, three hours, and my legs are toast.
Recovery right after is a big glass of chocolate milk, which is honestly the best part of the day.
And dinner is a huge bowl of pasta with a tomato and lentil sauce, lots of parmesan, and a side salad that I'll pretend I'm going to finish.
I added it all up, and today was around thirty-four hundred calories, which sounds like a lot, but I burned a lot.
The biggest lesson for me has been, under-eating on hard days makes everything worse, sleep, mood, the next workout, all of it.
So eat, please, especially if you're training this much.
And thank you again to Oatbound for sponsoring today's video.
If you want to try the protein oats, code PRIYA20 still gets you twenty percent off at oatbound.com.
Next week I'm doing my first open water swim of the season, wish me luck, and I'll see you then.
